proposals.title: Monorepo scaffold, strict TypeScript toolchain, and blocking lint gates
proposals.why_now: The repository has been empty for at least 8 prior cycles. Every subsequent proposal is blocked until a buildable workspace exists with the directory structure from §14.4, TypeScript strict mode with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, the determinism lint (blocking Math.random, Date, performance.now, Math.sin/cos/exp/log/pow/sqrt, float literals on economic values, sort without comparator, console, fetch, and all Node/Electron imports in pure packages by negation default as required by §13), and the dependency-boundary lint enforcing the DAG from §14.5. The FASE-1 acceptance criteria explicitly require these lint gates active and blocking before any other acceptance criteria can be evaluated. Without them, every subsequent package will silently violate ADR-002, ADR-003, ADR-004, or INV-26 in ways that cannot be corrected locally later.

proposals.title: packages/core — branded numeric types, positional RNG (with ADR), CanonicalEncoder (per ADR-009), and explicit rounding arithmetic
proposals.why_now: All other packages import core. The branded types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate as bigint; Tick and indices as safe-integer number) are the compiler-enforced mechanism for ADR-003. The explicit rounding helper is the mechanism for ADR-004 — the DEFINIR enforcement mechanism must be resolved in an ADR before any arithmetic code is written. The positional rand() function is the root of all determinism; the hash algorithm is DEFINIR and must be specified bit-exactly in an ADR before any implementation, because changing it after reference StateHashes exist requires an encodingVersion bump. ADR-009 explicitly requires the CanonicalEncoder to be implemented before any state hash exists. These are the first three DEFINIR items that must be resolved and implemented to unblock every downstream package.

proposals.title: packages/world — deterministic price generator for two assets with two noise octaves
proposals.why_now: The price generator is a FASE-1 hard requirement and the most algorithmically complex piece of the foundation. INV-02 (direct tick query equals tick-by-tick advance) is described by the spec as the most important test in the project. Getting positional sampling wrong retroactively invalidates all determinism guarantees. The transcendental functions log and exp required by §5.1 are prohibited in pure packages by §13 — they must be implemented as fixed-point or lookup-table approximations with bit-identical output across platforms, which requires its own ADR before any price code is written. The number of octaves, periods, and amplitudes are DEFINIR and must be fixed in a versioned config file before implementation so that subsequent parameter changes trigger encodingVersion bumps.

proposals.title: packages/domain — double-entry ledger and spot market order
proposals.why_now: The ledger is the other major FASE-1 prerequisite alongside the price generator. INV-04 through INV-07 (per-commodity transaction balance, zero-sum BRL, zero-sum per asset, rounding residue accounting) must all be green for FASE-1 acceptance. These invariants are best established while the ledger is minimal, before derivatives and liquidation add complexity. The domain package is also the first place where the bigint arithmetic and explicit rounding from packages/core are exercised in economically meaningful operations, making it the earliest integration test of core correctness.

proposals.title: Canonical tick loop, save format (ADR-006), tools/replay, and minimal Electron UI — completing FASE-1
proposals.why_now: Once core, world, and domain are in place, this final integration step closes FASE-1. The canonical ten-step tick processing order from §7 must be implemented in a single legible function with a test verifying step order — this is the most critical integration point and the locus of the most dangerous retroactive failures. The save format (ADR-006) plus tools/replay enables INV-01. tools/bench with frozen calibration ratios establishes the performance baseline gate. The minimum Electron installer is a hard FASE-1 requirement per §14.6 — the spec explicitly states that a deferred installer reveals ABI and packaging failures too late to fix architecturally. Without this, no FASE-1 acceptance criterion can be signed off.

warnings: Hash function is a DEFINIR item (ADR-002): an ADR specifying the exact bit-level algorithm (SplitMix64 over FNV-1a accumulator is the recommended starting point) must be written and approved before rand() in packages/core is implemented. Any change to the hash function after reference StateHashes exist requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates all CI reference hashes.

Rounding-mode enforcement mechanism is a DEFINIR item (ADR-004): an ADR must specify how calling division without an explicit mode is made a compile error or blocking lint error before any arithmetic helpers are implemented. Without this, the compiler cannot enforce ADR-004 and violations accumulate silently.

The price generator in §5.1 constructs prices in log-space, requiring log and exp. Both are prohibited in pure packages by §13. Fixed-point or lookup-table implementations with bit-identical cross-platform output must be specified in an ADR before packages/world begins; otherwise the price generator violates §13 or INV-19.

Octave count, periods, and amplitudes for trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise are DEFINIR (§5.1). These parameters must be fixed in a versioned config file in an ADR before the price generator is implemented, because changing any parameter after the performance baseline is frozen requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates all reference StateHashes.
SPEC_BLOCKERS.md does not exist. §19 requires this file to track contradictions and blockers. It must be created as part of the monorepo scaffold even before any blockers are known.
